input.betaBTitle: Reduction of the section modulus for U-piles without full shear force transfer in the interlocks; 1.0 for Z-piles

col.khTitle: Horizontal modulus of subgrade reaction; user input
col.undrainedTitle: Calculate this layer undrained with cu

input.customEi: Bending stiffness EI per m of wall
input.customHint: Bending stiffness and moment resistance (design value) differ per supplier and per section: take them from the product data. For plastics this includes the long-term value. A shear force of 0 skips that check.
input.customM: Moment resistance per m of wall
input.customV: Shear resistance per m of wall
input.factorsHint: The sets are a proposal and have not been checked against the text of NEN 9997-1 and CUR 166. Check the factors, the allowance on the retained height and the water levels for your reliability class and adjust them.
input.groundLow: Ground level low side, before excavation
input.kcrTitle: Crack factor on the width for shear
input.kindPlank: Bank revetment: continuous wall of planks
input.kmodTitle: Service class 3 (wet): 0.50 permanent, 0.55 long-term, 0.65 medium-term, 0.70 short-term
input.layersHint: The top layer extends up to ground level, the bottom layer to unlimited depth. You enter the modulus of subgrade reaction kh yourself, for example from CUR 166 table 3.3: this calculation sheet does not provide table values for it and uses one constant per layer. A proposal from the CPT is indicative and leaves kh open.
input.lowSame: Low side has the same layers
input.materialCustom: Plastic, concrete or other: user-defined values
input.methodAuto: Planar slip surface up to δ = φ′/3, curved above that
input.postSize: Diameter or side of the post
input.postsHint: The boards transfer the earth and water pressure over the centre-to-centre spacing to the posts; below the boards the soil acts on the post only. For the passive resistance of a single post the literature uses a width greater than the post itself: Broms (1964) uses three times the post width in cohesionless soil. Choose the factor for your soil and post spacing; the boards are always calculated as timber.
input.situationHint: Retained height {{h}} m; with design values the level on the low side lies {{da}} m lower, at NAP {{nap}} m.
input.spatialTitle: Below the boards the passive resistance and the subgrade reaction count over this factor times the post width, not more than the centre-to-centre spacing
input.supportAngleTitle: Downwards positive; 0° is a strut towards the low side
input.supportStiffnessTitle: Axial stiffness E·A/L of one anchor or strut
input.timberHint: Check according to NEN-EN 1995-1-1 with fd = kmod · fk / γM. The default is a wet application (service class 3) with permanent load: kmod = 0.50 and γM = 1.3 for solid timber. The strength classes and kcr have not been checked against the text of the standard; check them and allow for decay at the waterline.
input.wallHint: {{name}}: length {{l}} m; EI = {{ei}} kNm²/m of wall; {{props}}.

result.anchorPerM: Anchor force per m of wall
result.blumNone: no equilibrium within the calculation range
result.compareAria: Spring model next to the method of Blum
result.compareHint: Blum uses fully active and passive earth pressure and a rigid support; the spring model mobilises the earth pressure according to the displacement. The results should be of the same order, not equal.
result.head: Displacement at the head
result.levels: Stresses at the characteristic levels (design values)
result.levelsHint: h = high side, l = low side; all values in kPa.
result.method: Method, assumptions and what is not included
result.method1: Spring model according to CUR 166: a beam on elastic supports with soil springs on both sides that start at the earth pressure at rest (K0 = 1 − sin φ′) and are limited by the active and the passive earth pressure; one modulus of subgrade reaction per layer.
result.method2: Earth pressure: active with the planar slip surface (Coulomb), passive with the planar slip surface up to δ = φ′/3 and above that with the curved slip surface according to NEN-EN 1997-1 annex C.2. Undrained layers with σh = σv ∓ 2·cu.
result.method3: Safety: design values of the soil parameters, an allowance on the retained height and optionally on the water levels; displacements with characteristic values.
result.method4: Steel: bending, shear force and axial force according to NEN-EN 1993-5, without corrosion allowance. Timber: bending and shear according to NEN-EN 1995-1-1. Plastic and concrete: against the moment resistance that you enter.
result.method5: Not in this version: staged construction and prestressing, more anchor rows, the three-branch spring (kh1, kh2, kh3) and the step-by-step scheme 6.1 to 6.5 of CUR 166 with low and high stiffness, groundwater flow, loads at a distance, sloping ground level and a sloping bed of the watercourse, vertical equilibrium, overall stability, the design of anchor, anchor plate and waling, corrosion, local buckling of cold-formed sections, creep of timber and plastic, the check of the deformation against a requirement, and bank revetments with an anchored post.
result.method6: Posts with boards: per m of wall with the bending stiffness of the post divided by the centre-to-centre spacing; below the boards the earth pressure over the post width and the passive resistance over the factor for three-dimensional effect times the post width. The board is a simply supported beam between the posts.
result.plastic: Part of the embedment depth at the passive limit
result.springHint: Moment at NAP {{m}} m, shear force at NAP {{v}} m (design values). Assess displacements with the characteristic values. The spring model converged in {{n}} steps.

steps.boardLoad: largest pressure on the board (soil and water, high side minus low side), at NAP {{nap}} m
steps.eMax: sum of the passive effective earth pressure between NAP {{top}} m and the toe
steps.eMob: sum of the effective earth pressure on the low side from the spring model with design values
steps.mEd: largest moment from the spring model with design values, at NAP {{nap}} m
steps.nEd: input plus the vertical component of the anchor force
steps.nLarge: greater than {{limit}}: the moment resistance is reduced
steps.nSmall: not greater than {{limit}}: no reduction of the moment
steps.noClass: no cross-section class in the library: elastic section modulus
steps.tAvailable: level on the low side with allowance minus toe level
steps.vEd: largest shear force from the spring model with design values, at NAP {{nap}} m

visual.noWebgl: 3D is not available on this device. The cross-section shows the same data.
visual.pending: The drawing appears as soon as the input is complete and there is equilibrium.
visual.sceneAria: 3D view of the sheet pile wall; drag to rotate, scroll to zoom
visual.sceneHint: The soil block is cut open: the cut plane is the cross-section, the wall projects in front of it. Pile width, wall height and plate thicknesses come from the section library; the flange width is estimated and the interlocks are not drawn. Orange: anchor or strut. Drag to rotate, scroll to zoom.
visual.sceneHintRevetment: The soil block is cut open: the cut plane is the cross-section, the bank revetment projects in front of it. Plank thickness, post size, centre-to-centre spacing and boards are to scale; the plank width is a drawing dimension. Orange: anchor with waling. Drag to rotate, scroll to zoom.
visual.sectionAria: Cross-section of the sheet pile wall with earth pressure, displacement, moment and shear force
visual.sectionHint: To scale. Against the wall the pressure on the wall is shown: brown the effective earth pressure, blue the water pressure on top of it; the dashed lines are the active limit on the high side and the passive limit on the low side. On the right the displacement (positive towards the low side), the moment and the shear force over the same height; the dot is the largest value.

warnings.noBlum: The equilibrium calculation according to Blum finds no embedment depth within the calculation range; the comparison is missing.
warnings.noCustomShear: No shear resistance has been entered; the shear force check is missing.
warnings.noMoment: For this section and this steel grade the library gives no moment capacity (cross-section class 4 or no section modulus); the steel checks are missing.
warnings.noShear: The library gives no web thickness for this section; the shear force check is missing.
warnings.posts: Posts with boards: below the boards the passive resistance counts over {{f}} × the post width. This factor for three-dimensional effect is input; check it for your soil and post spacing.
warnings.shearInteraction: The shear force is greater than half of V_pl;Rd: the reduction of the moment due to shear force (NEN-EN 1993-5 clause 5.2.2) is not included in this calculation sheet.
warnings.timber: Timber: the displacement is calculated with E_0;mean without creep (k_def); under permanent load in a wet application the displacement becomes larger.
warnings.water: The water pressure is taken as hydrostatic on both sides; flow under the toe and its effect on the effective stress are not included in this calculation sheet.
